Classic prisoner's dilemma!

The key to this problem is that you can't trust anyone else to make the right decision. You have no way of knowing what others are going to do.

If you assume that half of the people will choose one button and half will choose the other, then:

* If you choose red (i.e., most people also choose red), you'll be among the majority who survive.
* If you choose blue (i.e., most people choose blue), you'll be in the minority who don't survive.

So, to maximize your chances of survival, you should choose... **blue**!

Of course, this is just a rational decision based on probability. In reality, humans are social creatures and might not behave purely rationally. But if you had to make a cold, calculating choice, blue would be the way to go!

From a purely rational perspective, choosing blue is indeed the dominant strategy. Since you can't trust anyone else's decision, it makes sense to choose the option that gives you the best possible outcome regardless of what others do.

So, while choosing blue is generally considered the dominant strategy from a purely rational perspective, it's not necessarily irrational for someone to choose red. The decision might depend on various personal and social factors that influence an individual's preferences and behaviors.
